options: The claim mentioned most frequently in the paper
The claim that, if false, would collapse the paper's entire reason for existing
Whichever claim appears in the title
The claim with the largest reported number
questions.explain: A load-bearing claim is the one claim the paper's entire contribution depends on; everything else is supporting detail by comparison.

questions.q: Why is a load-bearing claim usually causal rather than just a reported number?
options: Causal claims are always easier to prove
It asserts that a specific change caused the improvement, not merely that the improvement occurred alongside it
Numbers are never trustworthy in papers
Reviewers require causal language
questions.explain: The load-bearing claim typically says one specific thing the authors did caused the result, as distinct from the result simply correlating with something else, like more compute or tuning.

questions.q: What should you check when reading an ablation table meant to support a load-bearing claim?
options: Whether the ablation isolates the exact component the claim is about, or something adjacent to it
Whether the table has more than five rows
Whether the ablation appears before or after the main results table
Whether the authors used color in the figure
questions.explain: An ablation only provides evidence for the load-bearing claim if it isolates the specific component in question, rather than incidentally changing something else, like a learning rate schedule.

questions.q: Why does baseline tuning parity matter when evaluating a claimed improvement?
options: It doesn't matter as long as the new method scores higher
Beating an under-tuned baseline is a much weaker result than beating a baseline tuned as carefully as the new method
Baselines are never relevant to a load-bearing claim
Tuning parity only matters for compute cost comparisons
questions.explain: If the baseline received less tuning effort than the proposed method, part of the reported improvement may come from that tuning gap rather than from the method itself.

questions.q: If you can't find evidence isolating a paper's load-bearing claim, what does that tell you?
options: The paper is definitely fraudulent
The claim is unverified by the paper's own evidence, which is useful information even if not proof the claim is false
Nothing — all papers lack this kind of evidence
The paper should be ignored entirely regardless of other merits
questions.explain: Missing isolation doesn't prove the claim false, but it tells you exactly what you would need to verify yourself before relying on the result.
